# buy API gateway

Start with a free `GET https://gateway.usebuy.ai/v1/catalog`. It lists the currently
available capabilities, request schemas, token contracts, and indicative prices. Treat
that catalog as the live source for discovery, but quote the exact `POST` body before
paying: the request's 402 challenge is authoritative.

The catalog exposes a disposable agent-browser rental plus 170 inspected Monid APIs: 19
for X, 36 for Instagram, 33 for TikTok, 22 for Reddit, 32 for YouTube, 25 for LinkedIn,
and 3 for flights. China Southern is intentionally excluded. The original eight data
routes remain short aliases; the catalog supplies the generated route and input schema
for every additional tool. Callers do not pass upstream credentials.

For generated routes, send the inspected input envelope shown in the catalog, normally
`{"queryParams": {...}}` for direct APIs or `{"body": {...}}` for scraper APIs.
Per-result tools also require an advertised `maxResults` bundle. That bundle is a hard
upstream cap and is not prorated if fewer results are returned.

For an agent, call `buy_pay_quote` with the catalog capability's URL, `method: POST`, and
the exact JSON body as a raw string. Show the user the selected token and amount before
calling `buy_curl` with the same URL, method, and body. Never automatically retry a
timeout or `settle_uncertain`; those responses explicitly report `retryable: false`.

For a browser rental, quote and buy `POST /v1/browser/sessions` with a
`durationMinutes` of 1, 2, 3, 5, or 10. Save the `browser.accessToken` from the paid
response and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the returned `statusUrl` and
`commandUrl`. Supported command actions are `open`, `snapshot`, `click`, `check`,
`uncheck`, `focus`, `hover`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `scroll`, `wait`, `get`, `back`,
`forward`, `reload`, and `screenshot`. Close early with `DELETE statusUrl`; the fixed
rental price is not prorated.

CLI users can fetch the free catalog with ordinary curl, obtain a 402 quote with an
unpaid POST, then make the approved purchase with `buy curl --max-amount <token amount>`.
The CLI cap is in whole token units; MCP's `maxAmount` is in atomic six-decimal units.

Every 402 for a `/v1/*` capability also lists one `celo-sepolia` USDC offer at the same price:
the sandbox (the partner routes under `/chainstack` and `/cencori` are mainnet only). It is
USDC only (no USDT or USAT on Celo Sepolia). `buy --sandbox curl` or `buy_curl` with
`sandbox: true` pays it with test USDC from an account named `sandbox` that the CLI creates
on first use; `POST https://gateway.usebuy.ai/v1/sandbox/fund {"address": "0x…"}` hands
out 1 test USDC per address per UTC day, and the CLI calls it on its own when that account
is short. The upstream call is real, so the gateway caps sandbox upstream cost at 2 USD per
day in total and 0.10 USD per payer per day and answers 429 past either. Test USDC has no
value; the sandbox is for trying a capability, not for production traffic.

The same host also proxies the SQD Portal for free, with no 402 and a per-IP rate limit:
blockchain data across 100+ chains for indexers. `GET https://gateway.usebuy.ai/sqd/datasets`
lists the datasets; per dataset there are `head`, `finalized-head`, `metadata` and
`timestamps/<unix seconds>/block` (GET) and `stream` / `finalized-stream` (POST a SQD
query). The catalog lists these routes under `freeServices`. The limit is 120 requests a
minute per IP with a burst of 20; every `/sqd` response carries `RateLimit-Limit` (the
burst, 20), `RateLimit-Policy` (`120;w=60`), `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`
(seconds until the burst is back), and a 429 adds `Retry-After`.
Every stream line carries
`header.number` (the gateway adds `fields.block.number` to the query if it is missing), so
an indexer that loses the connection resumes with `fromBlock` set to the last line's block.
